findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
findings.body: When an event has Google Meet selected but no destination calendar, destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` produces `undefined` and the subsequent `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` access throws. This used to be guarded by optional chaining. Events without a connected destination calendar can therefore no longer fall back to Cal Video and booking creation fails.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar integrations always use the first host's destination calendar
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` invokes each host credential with the complete destination-calendar array, but Office365 selects `[0]` rather than the destination belonging to the credential currently creating the event. Thus, for a collective event whose first host uses another provider and a later host uses Office365, the Office365 call can target the first host's external ID (or fail/fall back incorrectly) instead of that Office365 host's calendar. The same first-element strategy is used by the Lark and CalDAV implementations, so multi-host events are not correctly created for mixed/non-Google calendar providers.

findings.title: Only the first collective destination calendar is persisted on the booking
findings.body: The event now accumulates destination calendars for every collective host, but booking creation connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`. Later flows such as payment confirmation reconstruct the CalendarEvent from `booking.destinationCalendar` and the owner destination calendar, so they have no record of the other hosts' destinations. In particular, a paid collective booking that is scheduled after payment will create calendar events only for the persisted main host rather than all collective hosts.

findings.title: Google event attendee identity is taken from the first host for every host calendar
findings.body: Although the insertion calendar is selected by the credential at lines 147-155, the organizer attendee email is always sourced from `destinationCalendar[0]`. When creating the event for a later collective host, the payload still identifies the first host's calendar as organizer/attendee. This can cause incorrect invitations or organizer attribution for the additional hosts; the attendee identity should be selected from the destination matching `credentialId`.
